findings.issue_text: EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? performs a synchronous DB query on every embed request, replacing the previously cached in-memory site setting lookup, a per-request cost regression on a hot public-facing path
The extra DB query also runs per TopicEmbed.import call
Missing index on host column in the embeddable_hosts migration, causing full table scans for the lookup query
The lookup uses a non-sargable lower(host) expression that cannot use a plain btree index on host; a functional index on lower(host) would be needed
Unbounded EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host) query in the admin embedding endpoint with no limit or pagination, loading and serializing all rows

Migration copies host values without normalizing them (stripping http://https:// prefixes and paths), so migrated hosts never match the bare hostname in record_for_host, silently breaking embedding after upgrade
Migration crashes on sites that never set embed_category: indexing [0]['id'] on an empty result raises NoMethodError (nil['id']), blocking upgrade; fallback query has the same [0]['value'] fragility

EmbeddingSerializer uses embed: :ids without include: true, emitting only embeddable_host_ids with no side-loaded host records, causing the client's _hydrateEmbedded to yield arrays of undefined and the admin embedding page to fail rendering hosts

Shared-store _hydrateEmbedded regex widened from _id$ to _id(s?)$ affects every REST payload; the plural branch unconditionally replaces any *_ids key with mapped lookups (potentially undefined) and deletes the original key, silently breaking existing endpoints with foo_ids data attributes
TopicEmbed.import drops the category for imports whose URL has no matching host record (e.g., feed_polling imports), creating topics with category: nil instead of the configured embed_category
PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a published no-op endpoint: the server action persists nothing but returns 200, misleading API consumers into believing settings were saved
Fabricator file contents are swapped: category_fabricator.rb contains the embeddable_host fabricator and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the category fabricators

Host endpoints return 500 instead of validation errors: save_host indexes params[:embeddable_host][:host] without guarding, and before_validation calls self.host.sub! unconditionally so a nil host raises NoMethodError instead of failing format validation
Migration crashes with NoMethodError when the embeddable_host site setting has no matching category row, breaking site boot/upgrade
Match-by-name JOIN between site setting value and category name is fragile and breaks when the category is renamed
Admin embeddable_hosts update/destroy actions crash with NoMethodError (500) instead of returning 404 when the ID does not exist
save_host raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error when the embeddable_host param or host value is missing/nil
before_validation callback blows up on nil host, so the model's format validation can never reject a blank host
Migration interpolates untrusted host strings directly into SQL, causing failure on values containing single quotes and creating an injection vector; should use parameterized insert
Client saveChanges has no error handling (no .catch/popupAjaxError), so update failures are silent
Backend embedding update action accepts PUT and returns success without persisting anything (silent no-op), causing UI to report success falsely
delete action in embeddable-host component has no .catch, so destroyRecord failures are unhandled and the row stays in the table
Hosts saved with a port can never match in record_for_host because URI(...).host excludes the port, silently breaking embedding with no validation error
Deleting a category leaves orphaned embeddable_hosts rows (no dependent cleanup or FK constraint), causing TopicEmbed.import to fail during topic creation while host_allowed? still returns true

New admin controller specs (embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and embedding_controller_spec.rb) only assert class inheritance and provide zero behavioral test coverage of create/update/destroy, the save_host blank-category fallback, error rendering, or the empty EmbeddingController#update
update/destroy actions in EmbeddableHostsController will raise NoMethodError (500) when the id doesn't exist because host is nil, and no tests catch this

The PR's headline feature (editing host↔category in admin UI) has no client-side JS tests for the component, controller, route, or adapter, leaving host.save(props) payload construction and post-save Category.findById refresh unverified
saveChanges calls this.get('embedding').update({}), a PUT that the server ignores, so nothing verifies this does anything meaningful

The expandable_first_post? test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' is now vacuous: it lacks a before block setting embed_truncate, so it passes due to the default false rather than the absence of hosts, and production code no longer checks hosts at all
The data migration CreateEmbeddableHosts is untested and interpolates host values raw into SQL, so a host containing a quote breaks the SQL

The migration inserts legacy embeddable_hosts values verbatim (e.g., http://example.com) without the model's before_validation stripping, so they will never match record_for_host's lower(host) = ? comparison against uri.host, silently breaking embedding for migrated sites
The migration assumes embeddable_hosts[0]['value'] exists without guarding against the setting row being missing

Port-handling gap: the validation regex accepts hosts with ports (e.g., example.com:8080) and stores them, but record_for_host compares against uri.host which never includes a port, so such hosts can never be matched and embedding silently fails; neither behavior is tested

record_for_host case-sensitivity edge untested: lower(host) compares lowercased DB values against uri.host which preserves case, so an uppercase referer host like EVILTROUT.COM fails against a stored eviltrout.com value; nil referer and referers without a host are also untested

TopicEmbed.import behavior change untested for URLs with no registered host: topics now get nil category (eh.try(:category_id)) instead of SiteSetting.embed_category, and no test pins the new fallback expectation despite import also being invoked by feed polling

Store plural-hydration tests rely on a pretender mock that ignores the requested id (always returns fruits[0] for /fruits/:id), so the 'find embedded' test passes only due to mock-routing behavior and id-based lookup correctness is never verified

Fabricator file contents are swapped: category_fabricator.rb contains the embeddable_host fabricator and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the category fabricators, so file names lie about their contents

Migration inserts unescaped host values via string interpolation into SQL, causing SQL errors on inputs containing quotes and leaving partially populated state with no rollback path; should use quote_value/bind params or EmbeddableHost.create!
Adjacent s.value = c.name join in the migration is fragile — if embed_category was a slug or the category was renamed, all hosts silently land in uncategorized

Migrated hosts with scheme prefixes (e.g., http://eviltrout.com) will never match the new lookup because record_for_host compares URI(referer).host against stored raw strings; the migration bypasses the before_validation normalization, silently breaking embeds after upgrade

Fabricator files have swapped contents: category_fabricator.rb defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines the :category fabricators; contents need to be swapped back

EmbeddingController#update does nothing — it re-renders the same serialized OpenStruct and mutates nothing, so the client's saveChanges issues a no-op PUT that a maintainer will assume persists data; either implement the update or drop the put route, update action, saveChanges, and adapter update path

Embedding aggregate is an OpenStruct masquerading as a persisted model (id 'default') serialized through a has_many serializer, leaking a type boundary to the client written against a non-existent REST resource

Global adapter change in rest.js.es6 (ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type.replace('_', '-'))) mutates the shared base adapter for all models to serve one feature; should use a basePath/pathFor override in the local embeddable-host adapter instead, and the dash-normalization convention creates a trap for future model authors

Dead code in store.js.es6: hydrated || [] fallback is unreachable since Array.prototype.map always returns an array; additionally hydrated can contain nulls from _lookupSubType returning undefined for unknown ids with no guard — filter nulls or drop the dead fallback

EmbeddableHostSerializer redundantly declares id, host, and category_id as attributes and manually implements them as object.attr, duplicating default AMS behavior in three methods that must be kept in sync

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? performs a synchronous DB query on every embed request, replacing the previously cached in-memory site setting lookup, a per-request cost regression on a hot public-facing path

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes embed host validation from `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?(request.referer)` (string parsing of an in-memory setting) to `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`. `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` calls `record_for_host`, which executes `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, i.e., a database query. This code runs on the public embed request path, so it introduces a per-request DB hit that did not exist before, making the performance-regression finding verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The extra DB query also runs per TopicEmbed.import call

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff adds `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` inside `TopicEmbed.import` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). `record_for_host` performs a DB lookup (`where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`). Separately, host validation in `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` and `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` now calls `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`, which also calls `record_for_host` (another DB lookup). So a typical embed flow can perform an additional embeddable_hosts query per `TopicEmbed.import` invocation, making this a verifiable per-call query/performance regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing index on host column in the embeddable_hosts migration, causing full table scans for the lookup query

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates `embeddable_hosts` with columns `host` and `category_id` but adds no index (no `add_index`). The code performs lookups by host, e.g. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, which cannot use a normal index on `host` and will result in sequential scans as the table grows unless a functional index (e.g., on `lower(host)`) is added. This is a verifiable performance defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The lookup uses a non-sargable lower(host) expression that cannot use a plain btree index on host; a functional index on lower(host) would be needed

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` which queries with `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. In PostgreSQL a normal btree index on `host` cannot be used for a predicate on `lower(host)`; you’d need an expression/functional index on `lower(host)` (or store `host` normalized to lowercase and query `host = ?`). So the finding is directly grounded in the new code and describes a real performance/indexing issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host) query in the admin embedding endpoint with no limit or pagination, loading and serializing all rows

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddingController#fetch_embedding`, the controller builds `@embedding` with `embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`. This will load and then serialize every `embeddable_hosts` row for the `/admin/customize/embedding` endpoint (via `EmbeddingSerializer` has_many), with no limit or pagination in the diff. If the table grows large, this can cause unnecessary query/serialization work and slow or memory-heavy responses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration copies host values without normalizing them (stripping http://https:// prefixes and paths), so migrated hosts never match the bare hostname in record_for_host, silently breaking embedding after upgrade
Migration crashes on sites that never set embed_category: indexing [0]['id'] on an empty result raises NoMethodError (nil['id']), blocking upgrade; fallback query has the same [0]['value'] fragility

EmbeddingSerializer uses embed: :ids without include: true, emitting only embeddable_host_ids with no side-loaded host records, causing the client's _hydrateEmbedded to yield arrays of undefined and the admin embedding page to fail rendering hosts

Shared-store _hydrateEmbedded regex widened from _id$ to _id(s?)$ affects every REST payload; the plural branch unconditionally replaces any *_ids key with mapped lookups (potentially undefined) and deletes the original key, silently breaking existing endpoints with foo_ids data attributes

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Store#_hydrateEmbedded to match keys ending in both *_id and *_ids via /(.+)\_id(s?)$/. In the new plural branch it assumes obj[k] (the *_ids value) responds to .map, then deletes the original key and replaces it with a pluralized association key (e.g. foo_ids -> foos) containing the lookup results, which may be undefined/null if the referenced objects aren’t present in the payload/root. Previously, *_ids keys were left intact. This is a global behavior change for any hydrated object containing an *_ids attribute and can break existing endpoints/clients that expect the raw foo_ids array (or have foo_ids that are not arrays), making the finding a real issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import drops the category for imports whose URL has no matching host record (e.g., feed_polling imports), creating topics with category: nil instead of the configured embed_category
PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a published no-op endpoint: the server action persists nothing but returns 200, misleading API consumers into believing settings were saved

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds routes for `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` and a JS adapter/controller that calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` on save. However, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, EmbeddingSerializer, ...)` and never modifies any model or setting (and `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`). So the PUT endpoint will return 200/serialized data while persisting nothing, making it a verifiable no-op write endpoint as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator file contents are swapped: category_fabricator.rb contains the embeddable_host fabricator and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the category fabricators

Host endpoints return 500 instead of validation errors: save_host indexes params[:embeddable_host][:host] without guarding, and before_validation calls self.host.sub! unconditionally so a nil host raises NoMethodError instead of failing format validation
Migration crashes with NoMethodError when the embeddable_host site setting has no matching category row, breaking site boot/upgrade

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does `category_id = execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. If there is no matching row (e.g., `embed_category` site setting missing/blank, or its value doesn’t match any `categories.name`), `execute(...)` returns an empty result, so `[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError`. That would crash the migration during upgrade/boot.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Match-by-name JOIN between site setting value and category name is fragile and breaks when the category is renamed

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, it derives `category_id` via `SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'`. This relies on the site setting value matching the *current* `categories.name`. If the category was renamed after the setting was saved, the JOIN will not match, `category_id` becomes 0, and the migration falls back to `uncategorized_category_id`, causing embedded hosts to be migrated to the wrong category.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin embeddable_hosts update/destroy actions crash with NoMethodError (500) instead of returning 404 when the ID does not exist
save_host raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error when the embeddable_host param or host value is missing/nil

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host the code unconditionally does `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]`. If `params[:embeddable_host]` is missing, this will raise `NoMethodError` (`nil[:host]`). Additionally, even if the `embeddable_host` hash exists but `:host` is nil/blank, the model’s `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!(...)`, which will also raise `NoMethodError` when `self.host` is nil, preventing a normal validation error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: before_validation callback blows up on nil host, so the model's format validation can never reject a blank host

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb the `before_validation` callback unconditionally calls `self.host.sub!(...)` twice. If `host` is `nil` (e.g., `EmbeddableHost.new` without a host, or params missing `embeddable_host[:host]`), this will raise `NoMethodError` before `validates_format_of :host` can run. There is no `validates_presence_of :host` to prevent the callback from seeing nil, so the model can blow up rather than cleanly rejecting missing/blank host values.

matched_golden_ids: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same core problem: interpolating host strings directly into SQL (e.g., "#{h}") creates SQL injection risk (and breaks on quotes) and should be replaced with parameter binding/quoting. adjudication_records.issue_text: Client saveChanges has no error handling (no .catch/popupAjaxError), so update failures are silent

If the underlying update request fails (server/network/auth), this action provides no user-visible error handling in this code path, unlike the host `save()` action which explicitly `.catch(popupAjaxError)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backend embedding update action accepts PUT and returns success without persisting anything (silent no-op), causing UI to report success falsely

In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, the `update` action for PUT `/admin/customize/embedding` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and never writes anything (no params handling, no model updates, no site setting updates). adjudication_records.issue_text: Hosts saved with a port can never match in record_for_host because URI(...).host excludes the port, silently breaking embedding with no validation error

adjudication.rationale: EmbeddableHost allows storing hosts with ports: the model’s validation regex explicitly permits `(:[0-9]{1,5})?`, and the `before_validation` callback strips scheme and path but does not remove a `:port`, so a value like `example.com:8080` can be persisted. However, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` does `uri = URI(host)` and then `host = uri.host`, which returns only the hostname without the port. The DB lookup is `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, so a stored `example.com:8080` will never match a referer URL like `http://example.com:8080/...` (parsed to `example.com`). This would cause embedding to be denied without a validation error at save time, matching the finding.

The candidate describes the migration using execute(...)[0] when the embed_category setting is unset/blank, resulting in no rows and a nil element, causing an exception when accessing ['id'] due to missing nil/presence checks—matching the golden issue of crashing when no embed_category setting exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration inserts raw embeddable_hosts setting values (e.g. 'http://eviltrout.com') without normalizing to bare hostnames, so EmbeddableHost.record_for_host comparing uri.host against lower(host) never matches http-prefixed entries, silently disabling embedding for upgraded sites

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` copies each line from the old `site_settings` value directly into the `embeddable_hosts.host` column via raw SQL: `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. This bypasses the `EmbeddableHost` model’s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http://`, `https://`, and paths. Later, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` parses the incoming URL and compares `uri.host` (e.g. `eviltrout.com`) to `lower(host)` in the DB. If the migrated DB value is `http://eviltrout.com` or `https://example.com/1234`, it will not match, so `host_allowed?` returns false and embedding is effectively disabled for upgraded sites that had protocol/path entries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unescaped string interpolation in the migration breaks (crashes the migration) for any host value containing a single quote

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration builds raw SQL with `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Since `h` comes from splitting the existing `site_settings` value (`embeddable_hosts`), any host string containing a single quote will terminate the SQL string literal and cause a syntax error (crashing the migration). This is a real correctness bug and also an SQL injection risk within the migration context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration unconditionally deletes the embed_category setting with no fallback path for feed-polling imports: when the import URL's host has no EmbeddableHost record, eh.try(:category_id) is nil and PostCreator gets category: nil, so embedded topics land in Uncategorized instead of the admin-configured embed_category

Admin embeddable_hosts update/destroy: EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil for stale/garbage IDs, then save_host(nil)/nil.destroy raise NoMethodError causing 500 instead of 404 (reachable via two admins viewing the page simultaneously)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the code uses `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`, which returns `nil` when the record doesn’t exist. `update` then calls `save_host(host)` and `save_host` immediately dereferences `host` (`host.host = ...`, `host.category_id = ...`), causing a `NoMethodError` on `nil`. Similarly, `destroy` calls `host.destroy` without a nil check. This will produce a 500 error instead of a proper 404/RecordNotFound handling when IDs are stale/invalid (e.g., concurrent admin actions).

adjudication_records.issue_text: save_host does params[:embeddable_host][:host] with no nil-guard, so a request without the nested param raises NoMethodError causing a 500

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, the code does `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` without checking that `params[:embeddable_host]` is present. If a create/update request is sent without the nested `embeddable_host` key (or it’s nil), this will raise `NoMethodError` (`undefined method [] for nil:NilClass`) and result in a 500. The diff does not include any `params.require(...)`/strong-params enforcement or other guard that would prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost#before_validation uses self.host.sub!(...) which raises NoMethodError if host is nil rather than failing validation
matched_golden_ids: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core bug: the before_validation callback calls self.host.sub!(...) and will raise NoMethodError when host is nil, instead of gracefully failing validation. This matches the golden issue about nil host causing an exception.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Store _hydrateEmbedded plural branch: _lookupSubType failures for missing sideloads produce arrays containing undefined/null entries, since hydrated || [] is dead code (map always returns a truthy array)

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch (`/(.+)_id(s?)$/` with `m[2]`) does `const hydrated = obj[k].map(id => self._lookupSubType(...))` and then assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []`. Since `Array#map` always returns an array (which is always truthy in JS, even if empty), the `|| []` fallback is effectively dead code. More importantly, if `_lookupSubType` returns `undefined`/`null` for an id that isn't sideloaded, the resulting `hydrated` array will contain `undefined`/`null` entries rather than skipping them (unlike the singular branch, which only assigns when `hydrated` is truthy). This is a real behavioral defect introduced by the diff: consumers of the hydrated plural relationship will see arrays with missing-object holes instead of a clean list.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Store _hydrateEmbedded plural branch: delete obj[k] is unconditional, destroying the raw *_ids attribute even when hydration completely failed, making the data unrecoverable (singular branch only deletes on success)

adjudication.rationale: In store.js.es6 _hydrateEmbedded, the new plural-ids branch (`/(.+)_id(s?)$/` with `m[2]`) always executes `delete obj[k];` after mapping ids to hydrated objects. Unlike the singular branch, it does not check whether hydration succeeded before deleting the original `*_ids` field. If `_lookupSubType` returns null/undefined for any id (e.g., missing from `root`), the resulting array will contain nulls and the original ids array is discarded, losing the raw reference data. This asymmetry with the singular branch (which deletes only when `hydrated` is truthy) indicates a real correctness regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Store _hydrateEmbedded plural branch: pre-existing serializers emitting *_ids keys where the subtype isn't a hydratable model now get the key silently replaced with [undefined...], changing behavior for consumers reading raw ids

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded` now matches keys ending with `_ids` via `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/`. For the plural branch it always does `obj[k].map(id => _lookupSubType(...))`, assigns the result array to `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]`, and then `delete obj[k]` unconditionally. If `_lookupSubType` can’t hydrate that subtype (returns `undefined`/`null`), the code still deletes the original raw `*_ids` array and replaces it with an array of `undefined` values (or at least an unhydrated array), changing behavior for any payloads that used `*_ids` purely as ID lists rather than embedded relations. This behavioral change is directly implied by the new branch logic in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost validation regex allows a port (example.com:8080) which is stored but never matches in record_for_host (matches on uri.host excluding port), so embedding silently fails for hosts saved with ports; conversely plain hosts match referers on any port so port restrictions can't be expressed, and the UI gives no validation warning

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EmbeddableHost`, the validation allows an optional port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) and `before_validation` strips scheme and path but does not strip the port, so a saved value like `example.com:8080` remains stored with `:8080`. However `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL with `URI(host)` and then compares using `uri.host` (which excludes the port) via `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. That means a referer `http://example.com:8080/...` yields `uri.host == "example.com"` and will not match a stored `"example.com:8080"`, causing `host_allowed?` to deny embedding. Conversely, storing `example.com` will allow any port because the check ignores `uri.port`. This mismatch is directly verifiable in the diff and would be a functional correctness bug with confusing UX (no UI-side validation to prevent entering ports).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb have swapped contents: category_fabricator.rb contains Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while the new file contains the category fabricators, a maintenance trap that also silently relocated :private_category etc.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was replaced with a single `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` definition, while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category-related fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`). So the finding that the contents are effectively swapped/misplaced (and that the category fabricators were relocated into an unexpectedly named file) is directly verifiable from the diff. While this may not immediately break specs if all fabricator files are auto-loaded, it is a clear organizational defect/maintenance trap introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/embedding_controller.rb update action renders the serialized embedding with 200 without persisting anything (no-op endpoint), so any future setting on the embedding screen will appear to save while doing nothing; the route and client saveChanges shouldn't exist if the endpoint has no behavior

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, the `update` action is indeed a no-op (it just re-renders the serialized `@embedding`, which is an `OpenStruct`, and does not persist anything). However, in the provided diff the embedding UI (`admin/templates/embedding.hbs`) does not call `saveChanges` or hit this endpoint at all; all real changes (create/update/destroy) are done via the `EmbeddableHost` model/controller (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`) and the `embeddable-host` component’s `host.save()` / `destroyRecord()`. So the finding’s impact statement (“the embedding screen will appear to save while doing nothing”) is not verifiable from this diff; it’s largely speculative about future settings/UX. The endpoint/action may be redundant, but redundancy alone isn’t a clear defect here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_spec.rb 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' test passes vacuously: with zero hosts fabricated, SiteSetting.embed_truncate? is false by default so eq(false) holds for the wrong reason, and the test no longer exercises the embeddable-host condition at all, providing no signal about the production behavior change where hosts can be fully deleted and first-post expansion stays enabled

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally removes the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` guard from `Topic#expandable_first_post?` (now only `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`). Since `embeddable_hosts` is no longer a site setting (it’s migrated to the `EmbeddableHost` table and access checks moved to `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`), a test asserting behavior when “embeddable_host is blank” would no longer be a meaningful production invariant. Also, the provided diff snippet does not actually show the referenced `topic_spec.rb` example (“is false if embeddable_host is blank”) or its assertions, so the claim that it “passes vacuously” cannot be verified from the shown changes. The alleged production problem (“hosts can be deleted and first-post expansion stays enabled”) is a consequence of the deliberate logic change and is not clearly a defect in the diff.
